title: 📊 Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit
rawNotionMarkup: Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age — creator-approved sixfold resimulation. This is the current demographic arithmetic reference replacing older population tables. All geography, peoples, city names and prior figures are preserved as an auditable baseline. Exact within-kingdom density and settlement footprints remain revisable. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age, intending first to besiege the dwarven Khazari strongholds and then to attack Eldar and human kingdoms. Their exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, first Orc communities, degree of subsequent mage control and actual military results remain UNDECIDED. No Orc inhabitants, settlements, armies or history can occur in the Second Age's Awakening (Years 1–321), Wonder (Years 322–1,321) or Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), or the First Age. Earlier lore placing Orcs there is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. Ambition does not prove these sieges or attacks were carried out; later Orc peoples have distinct cultures, agency and moral variation. CREATOR CANON — Orc creation by the Southern Wastes dark mages: The dark mages created the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and their volcano in the Second Age's Era of Fire, restrained its quake-amplified power at that Age's end (unknowingly strengthening themselves), then survived into the Third Age. During the Third Age they created the Orcs by an as-yet-undecided method, to advance their ambition to besiege Khazari strongholds first and eventually attack Eldar and human kingdoms. The intention and creator–creation relationship are now settled; exact date, process, locations, numbers, later power structure and whether specific attacks succeeded or even took place are not. The mages' isolation means no established diplomatic alliances, trade or treaties with previously existing outside peoples, not that they never created a new people. Modern Urakai are not collectively evil or automatically controlled by the ancient mages. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Canon worldwide totals Former worldwide simulated population: 343.8 million. New worldwide simulated population: 2,062.8 million (2.0628 billion). Continental total: Avarra 1,019.760m; Tharvorn 171.000m; Sahrad 282.222m; Orundel 393.600m; Vaelora 196.218m. This sums to 2,062.8m and excludes uncensused peoples. Khazari: former 24m global → 144m current; Seven Thrones domain subtotal former 22m → 132m, INCLUDED in the global 144m; Karak-Varn 3.8m → 22.8m, INCLUDED within the Seven Thrones. Most remote wilderness and severe climates remain sparsely inhabited. Eldar and Khazari and other established long-lived peoples are NOT given human-style rapid reproductive booms to justify their sixfold rescaled current totals. Their numbers arise from long continuity and mature institutions across an ancient multi-Age world. Smaller/shorter-lived cultures can experience periods of local prosperity and strain, but neither guaranteed overpopulation nor guaranteed stability is an inherent species trait. Count exceptions: Drakari, Aelwyn and Living Mountains lacking reliable censuses stay unquantified; ancient First Throne peak estimates and disasters are historical data, NOT modern figures to multiply. Undocumented unnamed places remain open for contextual world simulation. No live calendar, in-world population explosion, divine intervention or fate of Gloin has been changed. ## Source and priority The original Living Atlas I, II, III and VI census figures were preliminary scale models; this ledger is the new numerical authority for Year 3847, with originals retained in their respective chapters as historical baselines. Follow the new creator-approved demographic scale; don't use contradictory legacy figures as current counts. The core parent compendium remains Eryndor Compendium — Edition II (Provisional Audit, 20 Nov 2026). Its accepted geography, 50,000-km diameter, 60% water/40% land, Twin Titans land shares, Fifth Age, lunar theology and all paused campaign continuity still apply.
